newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to import more than 3 mln T oilseeds in '97.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to import more than 3 mln T oilseeds in '97.

text.p: Mexico is seen importing more than 3 million tonnes of oilseeds in 1997, the local offices of the American Soybean Association (ASA) and United Soybean Board (USB) said Thursday.
"Total consumption of vegetable oils in Mexico is about 1.4 million tonnes," they said in an update.

"If around 250,510 tonnes are produced from locally grown oilseeds and coconut, then Mexico will have to import the equivalent of about 1.15 million tonnes of oil in the form of seed and some oil," they added, calculating this would be more than 3 million tonnes of oilseeds.

The figure for oil output from locally grown seed (soybeans, safflower, cotton, coconut and corn) came from the ASA's own estimates combined with others from the Guadalajara Oil Crushers' Association.
"Of course, there is some hectarage in Mexico in sunflower, sesame and olive. About 3.5 percent of total oil consumption is corn," the ASA and USB said.
"Some crushers still experiment with canola from Canada and there will probably be about 500,000 tonnes imported this year, " they added.
"There is a government program underway to develop palm oil cultivation and processing in Mexico, but we do not see serious interest from investors in this program.

"Therefore, soybean, cotton, safflower and canola will continue to be the major oils in Mexico, with soybean by far the most important with about 25 percent of total vegetable oil consumption," they said.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom +525 7289530)) E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
